# Report Cites Benchmarks Rather Than Reproducing

**Decision.** Scope [[research-methodologies-open-set-recognition]] as a written synthesis. Take the
OpenGAN benchmark table from the source paper, label it as second-hand in the same view as the
numbers, and run no experiments.

**Date.** Committed 2026-07-11, in the commit that wrote the main report.

## Why

The report states the boundary directly beneath the results table, where a reader meets the numbers
rather than in a footnote:

> "These are literature results reported by the OpenGAN authors, reproduced here to explain the"
> — Research Methodologies/README.md, 2026-07-11

> "method — not experiments run for this coursework."
> — Research Methodologies/README.md, 2026-07-11

The `NOTICE` ledger says it a second time and the licence footer a third — see
[[provenance-notice-file]]. Even the chart is marked "redrawn", not reproduced: the figure is the
authors' own drawing of someone else's data, and the distinction is kept.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Reproduce OpenGAN on MNIST / CIFAR-10** | a training pipeline, a frozen backbone, GPU time, and the model-selection step the paper says is the difference between state-of-the-art and random — far outside a written coursework deliverable |
| **Present the numbers unattributed** | the failure mode this decision exists to prevent: a reader takes cited results for the authors' own |
| **Drop the benchmark table** | removes the one quantitative claim the argument rests on; the report would assert OpenGAN wins with no figure at all |
| **Reproduce a cheaper baseline (softmax / OpenMax) for comparison** | would have given one independently-run number to anchor the cited ones — not taken, and not discussed |

## What the decision costs

Nothing in the study independently checks anything it reports. The entire results section — MNIST
99.9, SVHN 98.8, CIFAR-10 97.3, TinyImageNet 90.7 — rests on **one** source: Kong & Ramanan's Table
1. Contrast [[convergent-evidence]], where a conclusion is only accepted once independent lines
agree. Here the claim is single-source **and labelled as such**, which is the honest version of a
weak evidence base rather than a fix for it. Recorded as the central limitation of
[[literature-review-synthesis]] as practised in this repo.

The cost lands hardest on the one place the study is arguing something: [[open-set-recognition]]
also quotes the Vaze et al. finding that a good closed-set classifier is already a good open-set
detector, which implies the softmax and OpenMax baselines in that table could themselves be lifted.
With no run of its own, the study cannot tell whether OpenGAN's margin survives a stronger
baseline. Both claims are printed; neither is resolved.
